subject: Deployment model constraints for PHI ingest — BrightLeaf Health (next steps & evidence)
messages:
From: krthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment model constraints for PHI ingest — BrightLeaf Health (next steps & evidence)

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion about your ingestion patterns and the regulatory controls you need. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can pin the deployment option that meets BrightLeaf's security obligations.

Recap (from our notes)
- Data type: patient-identifiable clinical notes + lab results (PHI).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~250 requests/minute; spikes to ~1k in batch windows.
- Retention: logs & prompts retained for 90 days by product team; security wants proof of retention configuration and purge processes.
- Audit needs: quarterly audit trail exports + SOC2 evidence for any vendor handling PHI.
- Primary concern: where PHI lives (hosted mem/disk) and legal guardrails (BAA).

Redwood deployment options and immediate fit
- Hosted API: fastest, but for PHI we typically require a signed BAA and may need logical/data separation; additional controls around KMS and egress. Hosted can work if BrightLeaf is comfortable with Redwood-managed key material under a BAA and the throughput profile fits reserved tier.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation. Good middle-ground — gives you predictable throughput and stronger isolation guarantees; can be combined with our managed BAA and customer-managed KMS options.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control (VPC peering or on-prem bundle). Recommended when customers require complete network isolation or specific audit hosting requirements (e.g., data must not transit public infra).

Evidence requests (what we can deliver quickly)
1) SOC2 summary and scope doc (we can provide a redacted summary within 48h) — attached: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf
2) Example retention/export process + purge runbook — sample doc link in thread
3) BAA template — we can share; if you require specific clauses we can route to legal
4) Deployment architecture diagrams for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (I will pull these and send by EOD)

Proposed next steps
- Alicia/Tom: confirm the minimal acceptable separation (BAA + Redwood-managed KMS OK, or must you have customer-managed keys / VPC?)
- BrightLeaf security: send any mandatory audit/contractual clauses we need to account for (if you have a short checklist, paste it in reply)
- Internal: Marissa / Grace — can you prepare dedicated vs hosted architecture slides and a short cost delta estimate for the traffic profile above? Aim for EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — I want to keep momentum on this. If BrightLeaf prefers a whiteboard session with security on Wed we can schedule it.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): BrightLeaf_RFI_PHl_scope.xlsx (requested by BrightLeaf during call), Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf

From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@brightleafhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@brightleafhealth.com>, BrightLeaf Security <security@brightleafhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment model constraints for PHI ingest — BrightLeaf Health (next steps & evidence)

Hi Karthik,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from security:
- BAA: mandatory. We can accept Redwood-managed KMS only if the BAA explicitly states key custody boundaries and provides audit rights. If Redwood cannot give those audit rights we will need customer-managed keys.
- Retention & purge: must be demonstrable (proof of purge runs + immutable audit trail). Include sample exports format (CSV/JSON) and timestamp accuracy.
- Data residency: All PHI must remain in US regions; please confirm Redwood's hosted regions and whether Dedicated keeps compute in a single region.
- SOC2: we need the SOC2 report (redacted OK) showing coverage of change control, logging, and access controls. The summary PDF is a good start but we'll still request the report for procurement.

Next for us:
- I'll share a short checklist from our compliance pack (2 pages) in the next email.
- We are keen to see the cost delta between Hosted with BAA (and customer-managed KMS) vs Dedicated (same KMS choice).

Tom and I are available Wed 1–3pm PT for a more technical conversation that includes our InfoSec engineer.

Thanks,
Alicia
Head of Integrations
BrightLeaf Health

Karthik / Grace — quick notes for the packet we'll assemble:
- Action: pull full SOC2 report redacted for customer consumption. Legal has a template NDA / redaction pattern; I'll own the redaction and clearance with security. ETA: 48 hours.
- KMS options: confirm we can offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Hosted (via external KMS integration). Grace, can you confirm the KMS flow for Hosted (bring-your-own-key via Cloud KMS) and whether it meets BrightLeaf's audit request?
- Region: Hosted has multiple US regions; Dedicated can be pinned to a single region — note any impact on failover if pinned. Need the exact region names for Alicia (us-west1 / us-east1).
- Cost delta: I'll draft a high-level delta (monthly reserved capacity vs hosted BAA tier) for Karthik to include in the Wed call.

Also attaching our quick diagram set for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private that highlights PHI touchpoints. I'll upload to the Drive link and paste after redaction.
